_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: 20 + 4 x treated + 0.1 x (age - 50) + clinic effect (SD 1.5) + noise (SD 5)

agreement.claim: both engines report the same effect, CR2 standard error, Satterthwaite df and interval
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: at most 1e-10, R's clubSandwich against Python's written-out CR2 and Bell-McCaffrey df: an independent implementation matching the reference package. harness/clustered_examples.test.py shows the CR1-style sandwich (1.27) and the naive OLS SE (0.55) are both smaller than CR2 (1.33), and that the df (8.98) sit below G - 1 = 11.

recovery.claim: the treatment effect is close to the fixture's

calibration.limits: Twelve clusters estimate the effect imprecisely whatever the variance estimator; the tolerance still separates the effect of 4 from zero. Measured by harness/clustered_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99.
